page: Microsoft Azure E32-8ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The x86_64 architecture is supported by a 35 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512. A key highlight of this configuration is its high memory density, providing 256.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 32.0 GB of memory per physical core. The instance also includes 1229 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, with no integrated GPUs.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the average tier for standard compute and memory tasks. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1272.0 and a multi-core score of 4842.0. Memory bandwidth is measured at 416.32 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 44.52 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak, landing in the bottom 25%, and medium-sized LLM inference is poor, with prompt processing on a 7B model reaching only 14.8 tokens/sec.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32:1 and the bundled 1229 GB local SSD, this server offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. It is highly suitable for large relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, and enterprise applications with high memory footprints but moderate CPU demands.
description: Microsoft Azure E32-8ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDSv4 family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs paired with an expansive 256.0 GB of RAM and 1229 GB of local SSD storage. Benchmark results show average performance across standard compute and memory tasks, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 4842.0 and a Redis throughput of 7.09 million SET operations per second. However, it exhibits weaker performance in multi-threaded decompression and medium LLM inference. This configuration is highly efficient for memory-intensive workloads, such as relational databases, in-memory caches, and data processing tasks requiring high memory density relative to compute resources.
